V2_budgeted_residency.result: HELD on all three arms, on the real container and on the bytes-backed miniature. The accounting now prices SEVEN resources by seven rules (`Resources`, `ResourceLedger::aggregate`): stored once per object, mapped address space once per mapping, persistent resident as the sum of committed allocations, transient as the PEAK, host touch per token as the image the executor streams, expected cold page-in per token from the mappings (top_k/experts of each bank access), device memory apart. A `ResidencyBudget` (physical bytes, optional `ThroughputBudget` in bytes per token) is an input to preparation: `select_realizations_within` re-selects, record by record, the largest resident saving among each operand's OWN candidates — reason `BudgetPolicy` — until the physical working set (resident + transient peak + page-in per token) and the per-token touch fit, or refuses before any payload byte with the deficit, the largest committed operands with nowhere cheaper to go, and every alternative already taken; `PreparedOperands::load_within` binds the re-selected pins. The observation side distinguishes a mapping's address space (`Observed.mapped_bytes`, held EXACTLY against the declaration) from the pages of it physically resident at that moment (`WeightRegion::resident_bytes` through `mincore`, reported beside the declaration and never reconciled against it); the census carries a `mapped` bucket apart from committed bytes.

V2_budgeted_residency.finding_V2-N2: The re-quantised images were priced per WEIGHT (Q4 at 0.5 + 4/64 bytes) while the loader blocks per ROW and never lets a block straddle one, so a matrix whose width is not a whole number of blocks carries a short last block with its own scale — the 32-wide miniature's Q4 image is 640 bytes where the constant said 576, and the first constrained-arm reconciliation refused on exactly that. Pricing is now the loader's own rule (`requantised_image_bytes`: codes per element, one scale per row-block, one sum per row sum-block when indexed), shared by the ledger and the budget's re-selection (`declared_resident_for`). The real container never showed it (k = 2304, a multiple of 64); the awkward shape did. It also exposed that the per-weight constant priced code sums per Q8 block where the loader keeps them per 16-element sum-block, a latent disagreement whenever the weight index is on.
V2_budgeted_residency.finding_V2-N3: Found by PR #428's Windows CI: `physical_memory_bytes()` had only a unix arm, so on Windows `ResidencyBudget::machine()` carried `physical_bytes: None` — the same value as UNBOUNDED — and the machine arm would have selected without a budget in silence. Fixed with a `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` arm (windows-sys, already in the lock); the witness asserts the machine budget is a real number on every CI platform. An unknown capacity must never share a representation with an unbounded one.

findings.V3-N1: The prepared CPU path executed a declared sigmoid router as softmax, folded the correction bias into the weights, and dropped `routed_scaling_factor` (2.446). Three planes: the checkpoint DECLARES `moe_router_activation_func: sigmoid`, `moe_renormalize: true`, `routed_scaling_factor: 2.446` and larql-models resolves them (`MoeRouterKind::Sigmoid`, `NormalisedOverSelected`, `branch_scale`); the PLAN carried the kind and policy but no branch scale (silent — the field did not exist); the EXECUTION plane's `select_experts` (production, shared by device) and `select_experts_reference` handled only Gemma4Hybrid specially and ran every other kind through the softmax rule with the bias added to the logits. The Kimi-specific executor (`kimi_router::route`) had the rule right; the generic path never did. Fix: `RoutedFfnOp.branch_scale` (from the surface, serialised only when present), `RoutedFfnCall.branch_scale`, `production::sigmoid_select` (scores = sigmoid; bias moves selection only; raw scores renormalised under NormalisedOverSelected; ties by index), a literal reference arm, and the branch scale applied to every rule's weights. Witness: exec/tests/sigmoid_router.rs against hand-computed literals — the two backends agreeing was never evidence, the miniature declares the same rule on both.
findings.V3-N2: Greedy-token agreement is not execution parity: with layer-1 gate weights wrong and hidden states 30–45% off in relative L2, the prepared plan still reproduced HF's greedy tokens at 4 of 5 positions. Only the intermediate tap (per-layer relL2 by position) localised the defect, and only the numpy reconstruction from the oracle's own taps identified it. [[feedback_execution_witness_needs_an_intermediate_tap]] again, at a new scale.
findings.V3-N3: Cold expert page-in is fault-bound, not bandwidth-bound: one 16 KiB page per major fault, ≈22 µs per fault (1.296 s for 0.976 GB, ≈1.1 GB/s effective; the prompt's 7.5 GB at ≈1.35 GB/s), an order below the SSD's sequential rate. The forecast's 2.944 GB per token is the DISJOINT bound; the first generated token paged in 0.976 GB because 67% of its expert pages were already resident from the three-token prompt (cross-position expert reuse in a short context).
findings.V3-N4: Residency has three states, not two: on disk (major fault, ≈22 µs/page), in the page cache but not in this process (minor fault, ≈0.8 µs/page), mapped in the process (free). RSS counts committed memory and the mapping's resident pages together; the latter ACCUMULATES across tokens (8.52 GB after four positions, 10.49 GB after the dumps) and is reclaimable. The budget's `physical_working_set` (resident + transient peak + page-in per token) is a per-token flow and a lower bound on RSS; the decision should treat committed + transient as hard and mapped-resident as soft.
findings.V3-N5: The warm token measured 430 ms in the first run and 140 ms in the second (same work, 0 major faults in both); the spread is not explained and is not a throughput claim. A steady-state protocol ([[feedback_bench_steady_state_protocol]]) is needed before any tok/s figure is quoted.
